sections.h2: Which sale route suits an Allen homeowner?
sections.html:
An Allen owner has three routes: a brokered listing, a private sale, or a cash purchase. Which one fits depends on how much time and repair work the house can take. Allen lies in southwestern Collin County along U.S. Highway 75, and Census figures put it at 113,447 people in mid-2025.

Owners occupy roughly seven in ten Allen homes, so a well kept house meets many buyers who plan to live in it. A home with deferred repairs, a tenant, or a probate delay tends to suit a buyer comfortable with the condition and closes when the seller is ready.

  • Brokered listing: the widest exposure, with showings, lender-backed offers and inspection negotiations.
  • Private sale: you set the price and run the showings, and you also draft the paperwork.
  • Cash purchase: one buyer, a sale in present condition, and a closing date that you choose.

sections.h2: How expensive and how crowded is housing in Allen?
sections.html:
Allen is a high-income, high-value suburb with a large owner-occupied base. The city's QuickFacts table lists the figures below, and they frame what a typical buyer or renter in Allen looks like.

The city's population count was 84,246 in 2010, so Allen added roughly 20,000 residents in the decade that followed. The 2020 density was about 3,963 people per square mile, a compact suburban pattern.

sections.h2: How did Allen grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
Allen began as a railroad stop. According to the Texas State Historical Association, an agent for the Houston and Texas Central Railway established the town in 1870, and it was named in 1872 for a former Texas attorney general who promoted the line. A post office opened in 1876, and by 1884 the settlement had a school, three churches, a chair factory and a flour mill.

Growth came late. The town had 1,940 residents in 1970 and 8,314 in 1980, a jump the Handbook of Texas ties to the economic growth of Dallas and Plano and the construction of Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. By 2000 the population had reached 43,554.

That history explains the housing stock. Allen is a commuter city built mostly in the decades after 1970, so most sellers are dealing with homes that are decades old rather than a century old, and the questions that come up at sale are usually roofs, foundations and updates, not historic districts.

sections.h2: Which Allen city rules should a seller or landlord know about?
sections.html:
Allen has recently added a rental program that matters to anyone selling a house that was leased. At its October 13 meeting, the Allen City Council approved an ordinance creating a registration and inspection program for single-family rental properties, covering houses, townhomes and duplexes.

  • Annual registration fee: $150, with a $50 late registration fee.
  • Reinspection fee for ongoing compliance issues: $25.
  • The city planned to begin notifying owners in November 2026, and the initial registration deadline is January 31, 2027.
  • The city says single-family rentals make up about 14% of its housing but produced 38% of property violations, which is why exterior inspections are part of the program.

The city is matching ownership and utility billing records to find rentals. If you receive a notice for a house that is not a rental, the notice explains how to contact the city. If the home has been a short-term rental, ask Allen's permitting staff whether a rental permit is on file before you list.

For remodeling and repair permits, Allen's Building and Permitting Division is the first call. Open permits left behind by a prior owner can slow a closing, so ask for the permit history on the address.

sections.h2: Who bills the tax on an Allen house, and what changes at sale?
sections.html:
Collin County's tax assessor-collector sends the bill, and the Collin Central Appraisal District sets the value. Statements are mailed in October, and the county's page advises payment by January 31 to avoid penalties. The Property Tax Office is at 2300 Bloomdale Road, Suite 2324, McKinney, and the county says tax certificates and similar special requests are handled only at the McKinney location.

Exemption paperwork goes to the appraisal district. Its FAQ says the standard homestead form is accepted January 1 through April 30, never before, never by email, and never for a fee. Missing the window is not fatal: the district allows a late filing up to two years after the bill went delinquent.

The district's 2023 table of rates and exemptions listed these entries for Allen city, and the current year's table may differ:

  • Homestead: 5.00% of value, with a $5,000 floor.
  • Age 65 or older: $50,000.
  • Disabled person: $25,000.

Older sellers (65 and up) holding a school tax ceiling can carry the ceiling to a replacement Texas home as a percentage, according to Collin CAD. A buyer who moves in files a fresh homestead application of their own.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded in Collin County?
sections.html:
The Collin County Clerk files Allen deeds. The clerk's land recordings page says to bring an original or a clerk-certified copy that is signed and notarized. It adds that House Bill 4350 led to redactions in parts of the online database, which is not the official repository of real property records.

Under Texas law, a deed has to be acknowledged before a notary or similar officer, or witnessed, before the clerk will record it. Fees vary by document and change over time, so request the current schedule from the clerk.

In most sales the title company orders the tax certificate, pays off mortgages and files the deed. Because a tax lien attaches each January 1, any earlier unpaid year must be cleared for the transfer to be clean.

sections.h2: What if the Allen house is inherited, in foreclosure or rented?
sections.html:
Three situations come up often, and each has a short set of Texas rules.

  • After a death: the court window for offering a will is four years. If nothing needs administering, a muniment of title lets heirs convey after the order and will are recorded with the clerk in the land's home county.
  • Behind on the mortgage: default notices give 20 days to reinstate, and a posted sale notice precedes the auction by 21 days or more.
  • Renters in the house: three days' written notice to vacate is the baseline unless the lease differs, followed by a justice court filing.

Closing before the auction date or before an eviction is finished leaves you more choices than waiting does.

sections.h2: What should I check before accepting an offer on an Allen home?
sections.html:
Put the following in writing before you sign.

  • A tax certificate from the Collin County office showing no earlier balance.
  • Confirmation from Collin CAD that your homestead and any ceiling are on file.
  • If tenants lived there, a check on the city's rental registration for the address.
  • A title search for open permits and unreleased liens.
  • The closing date and the fee split spelled out in the contract.

faqs.q: Does Allen require rental houses to be registered?
faqs.a: Yes. The Allen City Council approved a registration and inspection program for single-family rentals, including houses, townhomes and duplexes. Annual registration costs $150, with a $50 late fee, and the first deadline is January 31, 2027.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on an Allen home?
faqs.a: The Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector collects it. The Property Tax Office is in McKinney, and Collin Central Appraisal District sets the value and handles exemptions.

faqs.q: When can I apply for a homestead exemption on an Allen house?
faqs.a: File between January 1 and April 30 with Collin CAD. The district does not accept early or emailed applications and charges no fee, and a late application is allowed up to two years after the taxes become delinquent.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Allen house if property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes, but the taxes have to be paid at or before closing. A tax lien attaches on January 1 each year, so the buyer cannot take clear title until the balance is cleared.

faqs.q: What is the Census population figure for Allen?
faqs.a: The bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 113,447 residents, up from 104,627 in the 2020 census.
